newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end mixed after quiet session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end mixed after quiet session.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed a quiet post-holiday session narrowly mixed after bonds slipped late in the day and then pared losses before the close.

"A couple of trades" were all that was needed to push the March T-bond contract below minor chart support near 113-10/32 in extremely thin dealings. Some traders thought volume Thursday might not even be as high as the 20,000 contracts traded during the holiday-shortened session Tuesday.
"We're running on less than half strength," one analyst said of the lackluster dealings.
Traders said many participants had extended their Christmas holiday at least another day, and volume could be light through the New Year's holiday next week.
Short-covering pared losses by the end of the session, pushing the March contract above the prior support level.
U.S. economic data scheduled for release Friday is unlikely to have an impact on the market.
Jobless claims for the latest week are expected to slip to 346,000 from 351,000. November durable goods orders are forecast to rise 0.1 percent.

At settlement, March T-bond futures were off 2/32 point at 113-11/32, 10-year T-notes were 2/32 lower at 109-20/32 and muni-bonds were 1/32 higher at 116-06/32. March IMM T-bills were unchanged at 94.96 and Eurodollars were also steady at 94.45. ((--Chicago Derivatives desk (312)408-8750)) ((E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
